edges.description: The chimeric protein retains the CREB-family bZIP DNA-binding domain while replacing the cAMP-responsive, kinase-inducible regulatory domain with the FET domain.

The deregulated transcriptional program drives proliferation of the neoplastic cells. The effect is context-dependent: in engineered models the same fusion is lethal in undifferentiated stem cells and tolerated only in mesenchymal progenitors (PMID:34193943).
The IL6 promoter contains a CREB-binding (CRE) site, so constitutive CREB1 activation by the fusion drives IL-6 transcription.
Tumor-derived IL-6 drives the systemic inflammatory syndrome, which resolves after resection.

A proposed autocrine IL-6 growth loop. This edge is contested: a tocilizumab response in one case supports it, while another case had the inflammatory syndrome controlled by tocilizumab yet the tumor progressed.
The established tumor is the source of metastatic spread; CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion is a recurrent secondary event restricted to the metastatic cases.

nodes.description: The initiating lesion is a somatic chromosomal translocation that joins the 5' portion of EWSR1 (or, rarely, FUS) to the 3' portion of a CREB-family transcription factor gene. EWSR1::CREB1 from t(2;22)(q33;q12) is the predominant fusion; EWSR1::ATF1 from t(12;22)(q13;q12), FUS::ATF1 from t(12;16)(q13;p11), and EWSR1::CREM occur in smaller subsets. The cell in which the translocation arises has not been identified; the tumor is of uncertain differentiation, with a myoid (myofibroblastic) immunophenotype.
